Title: Technician Fourth Grade Marion M. Edwards having his picture painted by Japanese artist Takeo Hiroshima
Subject: African American soldiers;Edwards, Marion M.;Hiroshima, Takeo
Description: Technician Fourth Grade Marion M. Edwards, Charleston, serving with the 3160th Engineer Fire Fighting Platoon of the IX Corps, at South Camp Loeper, near Sendai, Japan, closely follows the ideal in his military bearing as prescribed by regulations, in the opinion of his commanding officer, Lieutenant Colonel Lloyd R. Moses, that the latter is having his picture painted at attention by a Japanese artist, Take Hiroshima, on a large plywood panel.  The panel will be posted in a conspicuous spot in the camp so that other members of the command will always have a model before them when they are turning over in their minds how they should appear whenever military courtesy calls for the portion of a solider at attention, such as when calling at the headquarters to make applications for a pass or furlough.  Sergeant Edwards lives at 5 Homes Street, Charleston, South Carolina.  He attended high school until almost the completion of his senior year when he went to work.  He entered the Army on December 27th , 1944 at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, and after receiving his basic training, embarked with an Engineer Company, and after receiving his basic training , embarked with Engineer Company for the island of Luzon in the Philippines.  On September 27th, 1945, his outfit was order to Japan. He wears the following ribbons:  Asiatic-Pacific, Japanese Occupation, Philippines Liberation, plus the Good Conduct and World War II Victory Medals.
